chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā and al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd and Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, concerning:

Regarding a man who incurs hadath after raising his head from the final sajdah and before performing tashahhud, he said: He turns away and performs wudu (ablution). Then, if he wishes, he may return to the mosque; if he wishes, then in his house; and if he wishes, wherever he wishes, he sits and performs tashahhud, then gives salām. And if the hadath occurred after the two shahadahs, then his salat has passed validly.

So the sound way regarding this report is that we understand it as applying to one who entered into the salat with tayammum, then incurred hadath forgetfully before the two shahadahs. In that case, he performs wudu (ablution) if he has found water and completes the salat with the two shahadahs, and repeating it is not required of him, just as he may complete it if he had incurred hadath before that, as we explained previously. It is also possible that his saying, 'before he performs tashahhud,' only meant completing the recommended tashahhud in full, not that what was meant by it was the two shahadahs, as we said concerning the first report equally.

key_terms.السَّجْدَةِ الْأَخِيرَةِ: the final prostration in the prayer
key_terms.الشَّهَادَتَيْنِ: the two testimonies forming the minimal essential declaration in tashahhud
key_terms.الْخَبَرِ: the report or hadith under discussion
key_terms.بِتَيَمُّمٍ: with tayammum, dry ablution performed in place of wudu
key_terms.يَتَشَهَّدَ: to recite the tashahhud in salat

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone incurs hadath after the final sajdah but before tashahhud in salat?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling for one who incurs ritual impurity near the end of salat, specifically after the final sajdah and before tashahhud. The compiler explains that the report is to be understood in a restricted way, either concerning one who had entered prayer with tayammum and then found water, or by interpreting tashahhud here as its fuller recommended form rather than the essential two shahadahs.
